text: - **Harness-driven tests:** the harness wraps any blitz_dom Document, such as HtmlDocument or DioxusDocument, with deterministic construction defaults, a pump/tick loop, `settle` (that pass repeated until no work is due, returning `Settled` or `NotSettled` naming the `Busy` class), inspection helpers and input synthesis (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/lib.rs:1-19), and since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot a paint with no display — `Harness::screenshot` / `screenshot_rect` into `VelloCpuImageRenderer`, composited over opaque white, at the harness's own time with no tick or pump (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/screenshot.rs:37-103), and since 2026-10-13-stand-contrast-harness a contrast reader — `Harness::text_contrast(node_id) -> Option<TextContrast>`, reading and changing nothing (no mutation, input, pump or settle; every node by `get_node`): the text-bearing element's computed `color`, font size and weight over the background composited source-over from its ancestors' `background-color`s onto the root-else-`body` canvas over opaque white, `None` with no text or where an element on the walk has `opacity` below 1, a filter or a background image, and `contrast_ratio` the WCAG 2.x ratio over the `color` crate's relative luminance (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/contrast.rs:13-23; packages/blitz-test-harness/src/contrast.rs:56-91); dom_string produces a stable one-node-per-line tree serialization with geometry, described as suitable for snapshot-style assertions (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/inspect.rs:117-131)

text: - **blitz-test-harness:** `settle.rs` pins the load counter — an answered request reaches the inner handler with its url and bytes and leaves none in flight, a handler dropped unanswered leaves none, the finished count grows by one per handler and never falls, `is_noop` is the inner provider's — the settle loop — an idle document settles in one pass, work for k polls in k + 1, work for ever ends after exactly `SETTLE_PASS_LIMIT` polls as `Render`, a request in flight after a quiet pass reads `Loads` after one poll, a handler finishing inside a pass costs one more pass, a wrapped HTML document is read through its render-blocking resources — and that every `NotSettled` message is non-empty, distinct and holds no `/` (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/settle.rs:193-462); since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot `screenshot.rs` pins the shot — the whole viewport painted at its device size, what the page leaves unpainted reading opaque white, a rectangle being that part of the frame, a rectangle past the viewport clipped and one outside it an error, a document with no font refused, and a shot the same twice (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/screenshot.rs:140-244); since 2026-10-13-stand-contrast-harness `contrast.rs` pins the contrast reader — `contrast_ratio` as the WCAG 2.x ratio over a stated table of 5 rows (21.0 both ways, 1.0, 4.48 and 4.39 within 0.005), `required_ratio` over a stated table of 5 rows (3.0 for large text — at least 24 px, or 14 pt at weight 700 — else 4.5), each row count asserted, and three fixture tests: a button reads its own text and background, a translucent ancestor is composited over the page, and an element with no text reads `None` (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/contrast.rs:200-308)

- **escher-driver:** wire.rs pins the closed grammar at `v3` (`v2` until 2026-10-19-session-recording, which added the fixed `ok v3 recording-failed` reply) — `hello`, `stop` and, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli, a third request, `call v3 <verb> [<name>=<kind>:<value>]…` (kinds `t` text · `n` whole number · `f` flag; the verb, the names and a text value percent-escaped byte for byte, the decoder strict), and the replies — the lifecycle's, `hello`'s carrying `idle_expiry_s`, and `ok v3 accepted <json>` · `ok v3 refused <json>` · `ok v3 oversize` · `ok v3 recording-failed` — round-trip; another version of a known word is `refused version`, anything else (a request line over 16,384 bytes, bytes that are not text, 51 malformed rows) is `refused malformed`, a reply outside the protocol does not parse, and a line is read up to its terminator and no further, an over-long or unterminated one named; a byte that is not plain is written as its escape, a decoded call equals the call that was encoded, the widest call the schema admits fits the request bound, and an answer at its 1,048,576-byte bound is carried while one byte over is not (a lifecycle reply is bounded at 128 bytes, the widest `hello` measuring 122); session.rs pins the label rule (1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9`, `-`), that an invalid label returns `InvalidLabel` without the boot closure running, and the session's record of ids — the ids read are held, a re-read id becomes the most recently read, and past the bound the one read longest ago is forgotten, on a record of a small stated bound; the bound counts ids, and since 2026-10-10-driver-cli the record holds no id longer than a call can name — an id longer than `MAX_ID_BYTES` is not recorded (`the_record_holds_no_id_longer_than_a_call_can_name`); error.rs pins that every `SessionError` message — the `NotSettled` arm's three, one per `Busy` class, included
 — is a non-empty fixed string holding no `/`, that an exit code is not in it and that the `Io` arm adds only the kind's name — the arm is spelled "input or output", since "I/O" holds a `/`; refusal.rs pins the closed cause set — eight causes in a stated order (`fonts-unavailable` the eighth, ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), each name, meaning and remedy a fixed text against a stated table, the remedies pairwise distinct and no `/` in any — and a refusal's printed form, which opens with its cause's name and ends with its remedy; schema_tests.rs (`schema::tests`) pins the verb table — twelve verbs in a stated order and three levels (`Level::Instance` · `Level::Session` · `Level::Tool`, `Level::name` reading `instance` · `session` · `tool`: the eight instance-level verbs, `screenshot` after `scroll` since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, `lint` after `screenshot`, then `start`, `status`, `stop`, then, since 2026-10-12-self-description, `help`), each with help, arguments and at least one result field, the lookup by exact name only (a name differing in case or padding finds nothing), each verb's argument and result shapes, the seven argument kinds with their bounds (the sixth, `ArgKind::Name`, 1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9`, `-`; the seventh, `ArgKind::Part`, a whole number 1 to `MAX_PART` = 1000), the field kinds, ten since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot (the seventh, `FieldKind::Count`; then `Words` and `Entries`, since 2026-10-12-self-description, and `Png`), and the twelve key names, so that an argument or a field of a wait would fail it, and, since that chunk, the thirteen node keys named in order, each with its help (`differs` after `bounds`), and the four exit statuses in status order; error.rs pins, since that chunk, that each of the session errors — fifteen since 2026-10-19-session-recording
 — states a kind, a meaning and a remedy and that the state directory's message states its bound (94 bytes on Linux, 90 elsewhere); since 2026-10-19-session-recording recording_tests.rs (`recording::tests`, in `recording.rs` until 2026-10-19-test-splits) pins the FNV-1a 64 digest of the written answer, a recording's read-back, the masked `type` stand-in, the calls no record can spell left out, owner-only modes with no file replaced and no foreign temporary removed, a recording ending at its bound or on a failed write with its check removed, and `Check::from_bytes`'s strict grammar (40 refusal rows and 8 read rows, the record keeping its answer, a shot's without `png`, edge rows at both bounds); since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay replay.rs that a check replayed on a fresh session holds, that an acceptance flip and a changed answer each stop the replay naming their keys, that a shot holds at its size whatever its pixels and that a check of another app runs nothing (packages/escher-driver/src/replay.rs:141-318); session.rs that a recording directory open to others is refused with nothing written and that a recording that ends reads failed once, and since 2026-10-20-load-wait the load wait over a scripted settle — a load answered inside the bound ends the wait settled, one never answered ends it at the bound still `Loads`, a `render` or `layout` answer returns at once, and a quiet settle returns after one settle and sleeps none (packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs:307-369); schema_tests.rs that the `settled` help states `LOAD_WAIT`, whole seconds, that the five acting verbs carry it and that the wait ends before an answer read (packages/escher-driver/src/schema_tests.rs:152-164); mcp_tests.rs that each session a recording boot starts is kept as one check and that a call that ends the recording is answered `isError` as its session error;

- **CI workflows and leg script:** test_ci_workflows.py — `CiWorkflowTest` pins ci.yml's `build/**` trigger, a rust-cache (matched by its `Swatinem/rust-cache@` prefix) with a `main` + `build/` save rule on every compiling job but the cache-less `coverage` and the restore-only `a11y` and, since 2026-10-14-quality-gates, `stand-repeat` (each carries the test job's `shared-key` and `save-if: false`), the fast four with no `needs` and every other job needing all four, each linux job's leg through `ci-leg.sh` (the leg present in the script's list), each leg job's own `if: failure()` log upload under `target/ci-logs/` kept 7 days (the coverage job's second upload success-only), no `secrets.`, no perl rewrite, the matrix platforms windows/macos/ios/android, every `uses:` pinned to a 40-hex commit SHA, every `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` step naming its `toolchain`, a workflow-level `permissions` of `contents: read` with no job grant, an a11y job named for accessibility, the coverage job's `coverage-report` upload of `target/coverage/` kept 7 days, and every package install bounded — no step's `run` naming `apt-get`, each step that calls `apt-install.sh` being that script and package names with no option (the `ci-scripts` one behind its PyYAML guard), the jobs that call it exactly the ten of `INSTALL_JOBS` (nine until 2026-10-14-quality-gates, `stand-repeat` added, as it is to `LINUX_JOB_LEGS` and `RESTORE_ONLY_JOBS`), and the one action step that installs packages, the matrix job's, carrying an integer `timeout-minutes` above 0 (`test_o_package_installs_are_bounded`, .github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py:218-235); `UpstreamGuardTest` pins the `DioxusLabs/blitz` repository guard on every job of publish-browser, wpt and wpt-post-results; `LegScriptTest` runs `ci-leg.sh` in a temp dir with a `cargo` shim on PATH
 — a failing leg exits non-zero and writes its log, the log is truncated at the leg's start, an unknown leg exits 2, the `doc` leg documents the whole workspace (`--workspace --no-deps --locked`), and the `audit`, `a11y` and `coverage` legs dispatch to cargo and write their log — since 2026-10-14-quality-gates the `audit` row asserting `--workspace`, `--all-features`, `advisories` and `licenses`, the `coverage` row two cases over a seeded lcov (the crates at their floors exit 0 with `3 of 3`, escher-driver one line under exits 1 with `1 of 3 … under`), a `clippy` case (the workspace line, then the blitz-dom line) and two `stand-repeat` cases (the three rounds; the stop at the first red) (.github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py:323-371) — the `a11y` row pinning all six test files in order, `accessibility_hidden`, `accessibility_roles`, `focusability_updates`, `stand_keyboard`, `stand_contrast`, `stand_accessibility_ids`, the last three added at 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions (.github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py:298-299); `InstallScriptTest` runs the CI install script `.github/scripts/apt-install.sh` in a session of its own, against a stand-in `sudo`, `apt-get` and, since 2026-10-14-quality-gates, `dpkg` first on PATH with the real `timeout`, and kills that process group when the test's own wait bound fires — eight tests (five until that chunk): a healthy install runs one update and one install, and no repair, a failed attempt is tried again from `update`, every attempt failing exits 1 after three attempts and never 124 or 137, a stalled call ends at its bound and is tried again, an install failed by its bound is repaired before the next attempt, a failed repair fails its attempt in phase `repair`, and a bad call
 — nine of them: no package, a name outside the closed form, an unknown option, an option with no value or a malformed one, `--attempts 0`, `--bound 0` — exits 2 before anything runs (.github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py:378-492; .github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py:422-456; the whole file's classes .github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py:103-496); four mutation controls of 2026-10-09-audit-corrections-agent-surfaces each turned a named test red and were restored with the file's sha256 compared — the script's loop cut to one attempt (three tests red, the retry test among them), its bounded `update` replaced by a bare `sudo apt-get update` (the stalled-call test red at its own 30 s wait), one workflow step put back to its bare `apt-get` line and the `timeout-minutes` line removed (the invariant red each time) — and the invariant read red on the still-unedited workflow, 11 failures (escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-09-audit-corrections-agent-surfaces/evidence/controls.md); the CI-scripts leg runs 100 tests over seven test files — test_ci_workflows.py's 33, test_wpt_diff_to_pr.py's 7, test_agent_run.py's 14, test_cold_agent.py's 33, test_wpt_area_changes.py's 5, test_blitz_tests_targets.py's 1 and test_coverage_floor.py's 7 — as measured at 2026-10-15-cold-agent-test (`ci-leg.sh ci-scripts`: `Ran 100 tests`, `OK`; test_cold_agent.py 27 → 33) and green at CI#38713461945 on `539defba`; 94, with test_cold_agent.py's 27, as measured at 2026-10-14-quality-gates (`ci-leg.sh fast`: `Ran 94 tests`, `OK`; +7 floor, +5 leg and +3 install cases) and green at CI#38692629940 on `d44090eb`; 79, with test_ci_workflows.py's 25 over six files, as measured at 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship (`ci-leg.sh fast`: `Ran 79 tests`, `OK`; +1, upstream #1183) and green at CI#38422391931 on `a6c24d24`;
 78, with test_wpt_area_changes.py's 4, as measured on the dev host (`ci-leg.sh fast`: `Ran 78 tests`, `OK`) and at CI#38013740580 on `9462a7e4` ("Test CI scripts"; escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-upstream-sync-agent-surfaces/report.md)

text:
- **Session ↔ held instance:** one `escher_driver::Session` booted through `seven_guis::stand` holds state, focus, ids, CRUD rows and timer time across commands and reads as a fresh boot, in both layout modes (tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_session_state.rs:56-169; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_session_ids.rs:52-141; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_session_fresh.rs:39-117); a step run through `Session::act` returns settled — the Timer's delayed update present, an idle step changing nothing, a write made while mounting present — or `SessionError::NotSettled(Busy::Render)` at the bound with the instance still readable, in both layout modes and with no sleep or clock read in the check (tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_settle.rs:35-174; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_settle.rs:277-312); since 2026-10-20-load-wait an acting step that meets a load in flight waits for it up to `LOAD_WAIT` (5 s of wall time), settling again every 10 ms and moving no time — `stand_load_wait` 2 through `Session::run` in both layout modes: a load answered at 200 ms ends the `click` settled with its content on screen, a load never answered ends it at the bound `settled` false with `busy` `Loads`, `harness().time()` unmoved in both (tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_load_wait.rs:107-164); a caller-built `Call` run through `Session::run` on a held session — `snapshot`, and `click` · `type` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll`, the first two and the last addressed by stable id alone — returns after settle with the diff of the snapshots taken before and after it, equal to the check's own `before.diff(&after)` and across the two layout modes; since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot a `screenshot` returns the screen, or the element its optional id names, as a PNG equal to the harness's raster and changes nothing — `has_changes` false, focus and the diff unchanged
 — an element shot's id refused `not-found` or `stale` and one cropping to no pixel `off-screen` with the instance unchanged, and a password typed through the driver never leaving as pixels (`stand_act_screenshot`); a refused call — any of the eight causes (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18, `advance` accepted on every session): `unknown-verb`, `malformed`, `not-found`, `stale`, `disabled`, `off-screen`, `covered` and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, `fonts-unavailable` — leaves the instance unchanged and reads as a text holding none of the bytes the call supplied, and for each of the five the executor detects on the screen a refused `click` and a refused `type` leave the snapshot and both focus readings equal; a `scroll` is refused for none of the three checks that stand in front of a click and says in its result whether its element is then in view — on the stand a CRUD row past its list's box is refused `off-screen`, brought into view by `scroll` and then clicked, the row's centre read against the list's `bounds` taken once, before the scroll — a scroll of the list's content does not move them; a password typed through the driver occurs 0 times in what the call returns and reads `MASKED_VALUE`; with no sleep and no wall-clock read in the checks — bar two recorded exceptions whose subject is wall time: `stand_virtual_clock`'s one 800 ms sleep, taken so a shot after a scroll is read to repeat across wall time until `advance` moves the fade, and, since 2026-10-20-load-wait, `stand_load_wait`, which reads `Instant::now()` around its call to measure the load wait against `LOAD_WAIT` and whose in-file `LateNet` stand-in answers from its own thread after a 200 ms sleep — and in the Timer flow no pass but the driver's; and with escher's sink installed at `info` each call run through `Session::run` — ran or refused
 — leaves exactly one `escher_driver` line holding fixed words and counts only (its verb, a refused call's cause, an acting call's settle reading and the three lengths of the returned diff) and none of the ids, names, values or typed text it handled, and at the default level no driver line — `stand_act_spans`, each reading made in a re-run child because the level is read when the sink is installed; and since 2026-10-10-driver-cli a `type` replaces what a filled control holds and an empty text clears it, a masked control's written form holds the mask and never the typed text (`stand_act_filled`), and since 2026-10-10-scrolling-box-bounds-and-hit the two engine readings 2026-10-10-driver-cli pinned are fixed in the engine and their checks restated — a scrolled box reads the same `bounds` before and after its content is scrolled, the scroll's diff does not name it, and a `click` naming the box lands on the row at its centre (`stand_act_scroll`); a button lying where a scrolled-out row extends is clicked, its handler runs and no row's, and after the accepted click the clicked button reads `focused` and is the tree's focus (`stand_act_obstructed`, restated at 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness); two readings stay as measured, each stated in `covered`'s fixed meaning: a box with no width or no height is hit at its centre on the element that holds it, so `covered` can read where nothing covers it (`stand_act_ids`), and a box clipped on one axis stops a hit at its whole padding box, so a target lying outside it along the axis it does not clip is refused `covered` though it shows, the instance unchanged, in both layout modes (`stand_act_obstructed`'s sixth test; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_obstructed.rs:560-605; packages/escher-driver/src/refusal.rs:74-79);
 and since 2026-10-10-snapshot-states an acting call returns the node it changed with its `selected`, `pressed` or `invalid` reading as it reads after the step — a flight-mode click both mode buttons with their pressed reading, a row click the row selected and the row it leaves not selected, a typed start date the field invalid or not — each diff equal across the two layout modes (`stand_act_states`); a `click` on a translated button is accepted and lands, and its snapshot `bounds` read where it shows, in both layout modes (`stand_act_transformed`; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_transformed.rs:76-116); a `type` on a single-choice select chooses the first option whose label starts with the text — accepted and settled, its diff naming the select with `value` in `differs` and the two options whose `selected` moved, the select's options read as its children named by their labels, a disabled select skipped by the Tab walk and refused, in both layout modes (`stand_act_select`; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_select.rs:79-256) (the fifteen `stand_act_*` files, §1) — as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-act-by-id/report.md, the three state readings at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-snapshot-states/report.md, the two fixed readings at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-scrolling-box-bounds-and-hit/report.md, the detected causes and `scroll` at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-refusal-detection/report.md, the command span's line at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-command-spans/report.md

subject: mocking
text: | Time (seven_guis timer) | `TimerTicks`, provided in context by every headless-stand boot, replaces the timer's 100 ms `futures_timer::Delay`: each `deliver(n)` tick is one 0.1 s step capped at the duration, applied on the next pass — a `pump`, an input helper's own pump, or a settle (`Harness::settle`, `Session::act`, each acting verb of `Session::run`) — so a delivery made before an input helper is applied by that helper's pump and one made after it by nothing until a later pass; settle neither advances the timer nor waits on a tick not yet delivered; an undelivered source holds elapsed at 0.0 s; the driver moves that time by `advance`, which moves the session's clock — the harness's `VirtualClock`, the clock every harness-built document reads — by exactly `ms` inside one settled step, then hands `ms` to the step: `seven_guis::stand::timer_step(ticks)` is the step the Timer's session carries through `Session::with_time` — it returns nothing and delivers the whole 100 ms ticks (`TIMER_TICK_MS`) the asks hold, carrying the remainder below one tick across calls (250 then 250 → 2 then 3 ticks); `advanced_ms` is exactly `ms`, the clock's move (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), not what the Timer's counter gained — 60000 is reported while the elapsed display stops at its 15 s duration | (examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/timer.rs:10-20; examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/timer.rs:47-55; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_timer.rs:7-46; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_settle.rs:35-76; examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs:85-102; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_act_timer.rs:1-12; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-settle-detection/evidence/red-first.md, the driver's `advance` at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-act-by-id/report.md, on the one clock at escher-0.2.0/chunks/2026-10-18-one-virtual-clock/report.md) |
